note: Rivals leaderboard-prep dataset. Structure: one entry per TRACK (metadata + inferred character + road-template link), each holding a class_analyses[] you fill in from an in-game leaderboard screenshot. Scaffolded tracks say 'awaiting leaderboard'. Read the board with board_reading_heuristic BEFORE trusting any top time; source tunes per the discipline template (road = low convergence -> download the fastest clean-lap tune).
scope: All 22 FH6 Road Racing events (12 Circuits + 10 Sprints), source: mapmaster.io. Character per track is INFERRED from the real-world location (🟡) until confirmed against the in-game layout / leaderboard.

board_reading_heuristic.purpose: Read a Rivals leaderboard critically before copying anyone or picking a target.
rules: CONTESTED vs SOFT: on a solved board the top ~10 sit within ~1-2s. A big spread (25s+) = SOFT board — car choice barely matters; a clean optimized lap climbs the ranks.
OUTLIER = SUSPECT: if the top few beat the clean-lap CLUSTER by >~10% of laptime, suspect a CUT/DIRTY lap the game didn't invalidate (most common), not skill.
AI/DEV SEED TIMES: names like 'AI Test#######' are benchmark entries, not real players — ignore as targets.
HACKING is the LEAST likely cause of a fast-but-plausible time; real hacks are absurd (sub-0:30). Console is locked.
VERIFY WITH THE GHOST: download the suspect ghost — cuts/teleports = dirty; clean fast line = legit and beatable.
PICK THE RIGHT TARGET: race the clean-lap cluster; use Change Filter -> Friends/Region + any clean-lap filter.
UNDER-PI CAN WIN on technical tracks: fastest runs sometimes sit below the class cap (grip/control > raw power).

tune_sourcing: Road = LOW convergence (see tuning-templates.json): download the fastest CLEAN-lap driver's shared tune from the leaderboard, or in-game Tune Browser > Surface: ROAD (never a raw car search — that surfaces drag tunes that can't corner). The road template is a starting point, not the answer.
scaffold_todo: To complete a track: send an in-game Rivals leaderboard screenshot for it + the class you race. I'll add a class_analyses entry (board read, recommended car+acquisition, tune source, targets).

tracks.name: Electric Town Circuit
tracks.character: Tight technical urban street circuit — short straights, 90-degree corners, walls close. Grip/braking/corner-exit >> top speed.

class_analyses.board_state: SOFT/uncontested (2026-07-10). Global top 11 spanned 1:05.127 -> 1:32.755 (27s). Clean-lap cluster ~1:28-1:32 at 700 PI. Top 1-4 are outliers (suspect cut/dirty; #3 'AI Test071831' is a seed time).

top.flag: SUSPECT — 8.5s clear; likely cut/dirty. Verify by ghost.

top.car: Supra '20 / BMW i8 / GR86 / City E II / Ford GT '05 x2

class_analyses.recommended_car: Toyota Supra '20 (RWD) — most-represented on the board (3x, incl #1 & #4); in the meta DB (gr-supra-2020).
class_analyses.acquisition: EASY. Autoshow ~45,000 cr (buy anytime) AND free via Journal 'Discovery' Tier 4. No RNG.
class_analyses.how_to_get_the_tune: 616 PI is NOT searchable (it was a bespoke under-cap build). Download the fastest CLEAN Supra driver's shared tune from the leaderboard (e.g. #4/#6), or Tune Browser > 2020 GR Supra > Surface: ROAD > A class > sort by rating. '616' just means grip-focused, not a target.
class_analyses.tune_browser_warning: A raw car search mixes disciplines and DRAG tunes are most-downloaded — a drag tune CANNOT CORNER (drag tires lost all lateral grip in the 2026-06-15 patch, locked diff, no aero: washes straight above ~30 mph). Pick a ROAD tune; check Upgrades>Tires compound isn't 'Drag'.
class_analyses.key_insight: CAR IS NOT THE BOTTLENECK. #1 on a 616 Supra beats a maxed 700 Audi by 14s — that's line + clean laps. A single clean lap vaults you from top 53% to ~top 10% here.

targets.stretch: 1:05 (#1) — verify it isn't a cut lap via ghost first

tracks.name: Shirakawa Circuit
tracks.character: Surface: tarmac/paved road race. Character: described by FH6 sources as "a short technical circuit with plenty of long, sweeping corners that keep the pace fast" — flowing momentum layout dominated by medium-to-fast sweepers rather than stop-and-go hairpins. No long straights, tight hairpins, notable elevation, or wall-lined sections are called out in any source. Located in the Minamino region near the Shirakawa-go village / golf course area (sources disagree on exact edge: mapmaster says northern side, one search snippet says near the southern edge of the golf course — minor, not tuning-relevant). Entry-level event, no wristband requirement.
tracks.length: ~4.0 miles total; 2 laps (~2 mi / ~3.2 km per lap). One search snippet gave "3.2 KM" which lines up as the per-lap figure vs the 4.0 mi / 6.4 km two-lap total.

research.caveat: The lone description literally leads with "short TECHNICAL circuit," so "mixed-technical" is an equally valid tightening; "mixed" is the safe center label. Real-world-vs-in-game mismatch risk is LOW here (the source describes a race circuit, and metadata cross-matches across three sources), but the driving-character basis is a SINGLE thin auto-generated wiki (game.wiki) — do not treat it as multi-source confirmed. The claim's stated three-source corroboration of the phrase does not exist.

tracks.name: Daikoku Circuit
tracks.character: Fast-paced circuit on extra-wide, expressway-grade asphalt (Daikoku PA / Wangan interchange setting) with big-radius sweepers and loop-ramp curves; wide roads give plenty of overtaking room. High average speed (~118 mph on an S1 rival lap) but still a cornered circuit, not a flat-out highway. Surface: smooth sealed asphalt; concrete barrier walls line the expressway sections. Some elevation change on the interchange ramps. Runs Spring / Clear / Morning with no traffic (distinct from the night Daikoku Chase street race).
tracks.length: 3.3 miles total, 2 laps (~1.65 mi per lap)

research.caveat: The "objectively fast ~118 mph" evidence is from an S1 Rivals lap, whereas the event itself is Class B-600; B-class cars would average notably less, so the raw-speed figure is somewhat inflated (the in-game "fast-paced/extra-wide" description supports fast regardless). The circuit sits on the real Daikoku/Wangan expressway, so name and profile happen to coincide, though the verdict rests on the in-game description rather than the name. A couple of low-quality content-farm pages (u4n, gamingpromax) describe it as "tight/technical," conflicting with the primary aggregators — they appear to conflate the circuit with the Daikoku car-meet island and are weighted lower.

tracks.name: Hokubu Circuit
tracks.character: Short circuit on the eastern coast of the Hokubu region (NE map), in forested/coastal terrain above a peninsula with road stretches over water near the Irabuohashi Bridge. Blends long sweeping bends with heavy braking zones and tight technical corner exits ("short and technical, corner exits matter more than top speed"). First two corners have noticeable undulation; final corner sequence is technical and satisfying. Elevation change throughout. Surface: sealed asphalt/tarmac, touge-style narrow road; walls not emphasized in sources. Braking, rotation, and high-downforce dominate over top-end.
tracks.length: 4.7 mi total, 3 laps (~1.57 mi/lap). Lap runs ~45-58s in a fast S1 car.

research.caveat: Two soft spots keep this short of airtight. (1) Real-world-vs-in-game naming: the claim's "Irabuohashi Bridge" is an author embellishment not found in FH6 sources — those only mention "three stretches of road going over water" near a NE peninsula; the actual Irabu Ohashi bridge is in Okinawa/Miyako (far south), which contradicts the stated northern location, so that specific name is unverified and likely wrong even though the underlying in-game "roads over water" feature is real. (2) Source independence is moderate: OverTake.gg and sippycupmom share near-identical wording (possible common or AI-generated origin), though ForzaFactory independently corroborates the technical/high-downforce angle. Given the strong flow-state / long-sweeping-bends language, plain "mixed" remains a defensible alternative to "mixed-technical."

tracks.name: Soni Circuit
tracks.character: Twisty, undulating purpose-built circuit with real elevation change. Opens with two proper corners, then DROPS into a hairpin (good divebomb spot), immediately followed by a corner too tight to get two cars through side-by-side. Signature closing feature is a long QUADRUPLE-APEX final corner (a flowing sustained sweeper). Explicitly "quite undulating" and "perfect for drifting." Paved/tarmac, has a pit lane/area; runoff-style facilities (no heavy street walls noted). Scenic highland setting with Mt Fuji and Tokyo views. Central/north Takashiro, north of Hokubu.
tracks.length: ~4.8 mi total over 4 laps in the Festival Playlist instance (~1.2 mi/lap short circuit)

research.caveat: Mild overstatement risk: the OverTake source itself calls the layout "relatively simple" and "big enough to go racing in any car," which softens the claim's stronger "sharp twisty corners dominate / clearly MORE technical" framing — "technical-leaning" sits at the top of what the source supports rather than being unambiguous. The specific "~1.2mi lap" length is the claim author's own addition and is not stated in any source found. Evidence is single expert-tier article (OverTake) plus corroborating listings/videos, not a primary/official route map, so confidence is strong but one notch below hard primary. The FH6 "Soni" circuit only borrows the real place name; there is no scenic-grassland real-world feature driving the profile, so no real-world-vs-in-game mismatch.

tracks.name: Narai-juku Circuit
tracks.character: Documented in-game description: "A quick circuit that favours an aggressive cornering approach to build momentum lap on lap." Community track review calls it "akin to a proper race track" and "a great practice/tuning area" (36+ laps run against unbeatable AI). Signals a flowing, momentum-preserving asphalt circuit where carrying speed through corners matters, NOT a stop-and-go hairpin track. Corner count, elevation profile, chicanes, walls, and surface specifics are NOT explicitly documented by any source found (surface is standard tarmac by Road Racing category). Located on the northern side of the Shimanoyama region; runs Spring / Clear / Early Afternoon.
tracks.length: 4.4 mi total over 3 laps (~1.47 mi per lap)

research.caveat: Real-world Narai-juku is a slow, narrow Nakasendo post town (Nagano) — a pedestrian street, not a race circuit — so there is NO real-world layout to lean on; FH6's circuit merely borrows the in-game place name. The profile therefore cannot be inferred from the real place and rests entirely on one FH6 database's character blurb, which is single-origin and, per this project's own June-2026 verification, much FH6 web content is self-copying AI/SEO text of unconfirmed authenticity. "mixed-fast" remains within the plausible range but is not established; "mixed" or "mixed-technical" are equally consistent with the evidence.

tracks.name: Shimanoyama Circuit
tracks.character: Purpose-built drift-style circuit: linked free-flowing / sweeping corners with momentum emphasis (can hold a gear through much of it), plus at least one tighter corner needing a braking/careful line. Short compact loop with some elevation change. Run with slow/quirky domestic + kei cars (Eclectic Domestics class: e.g., Honda Beat, Nissan Figaro). NOT a hairpin-heavy touge; no long straights/highway. Wall/surface specifics not confirmed by a source.
tracks.length: 3.4 mi total, 5 laps (~0.68 mi/lap) — a compact "Short Circuit" loop

research.caveat: Two sub-claims are weaker than the core finding. (1) The feature note "at least one tighter corner needing a braking/careful line" is NOT supported and is arguably contradicted: allthings.how states the layout "avoids tight braking corners." Treat that detail as unconfirmed. (2) "Mixed" describes corner VARIETY, not pace — because this is a drift circuit run with ~63hp kei/domestic cars (Honda Beat, Figaro) on a very short ~0.68 mi/lap loop, actual on-track speed is low despite the "free-flowing" wording; do not read "mixed" as fast. Real-world-vs-in-game note: the region's real association is with drift/jump spots, which happens to align with an in-game DRIFT circuit, but the in-game confirmation here rests on actual FH6 route sources, not that coincidence.

tracks.name: Irokawa Circuit
tracks.character: Loops around the Irokawa Space Centre on the southern side of the Nangan region (industrial/facility setting, NOT coastal). Defining element is a steep downhill section leading into a heavy-braking hairpin, explicitly flagged as the track's hardest corner. Short ~1.17mi lap implies several corners with some flow between the technical sections. Conditions: Spring, cloudy, early afternoon. No source confirmed long straights, sweepers, wall proximity, or surface transitions.
tracks.length: 3.5 mi total over 3 laps (~1.17 mi per lap, short lap)

research.caveat: Only ONE corner is described in any source (the downhill-into-hairpin); the rest of the "mixed-technical" balance is inferred from the short lap length, so plain "mixed" would also be defensible — treat the technical lean as probable, not certain. Also, the claim's "industrial/facility setting, NOT coastal" is slightly overstated: real space centres sit on the coast and Nangan is described as having coastal highways, so the Irokawa Space Centre loop may well be coastal-adjacent; the correction holds on driving CHARACTER (technical facility loop, not coastal sweepers) rather than on geography being non-coastal.
sources: https://mapmaster.io/games/forza-horizon-6/guides/Road%20Racing%20Event (describes the actual in-game route: circuit, 3 laps/3.5mi, loops Irokawa Space Centre, steep downhill into a braking hairpin, S1 800 Eclectic Domestics)
https://guides4gamers.com/forza-horizon-6/pois/road-racing/ (confirms event exists, unlock, Eclectic Domestics restriction; no route detail)
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ezcbAGZdfrM (Irokawa Circuit Honda Beat gameplay; title only, weak signal toward agility)

tracks.name: Highway Circuit
tracks.character: Elevated Tokyo "Highway Loop" (C1-inspired). Long full-throttle straights linked by fast sweeping/banked bends, tunnel and elevated sections, and highway on/off-ramp connector corners rather than slow hairpins. Smooth asphalt surface; concrete barrier walls line the expressway, so wall proximity/precision matters at speed. Minimal low-speed technical content per event description. Dry (Summer, Cloudy, Early Afternoon).
tracks.length: 2 laps, 8.7 mi total (~4.35 mi per lap)

research.caveat: The claim's detailed feature list (C1-inspired, tunnels, elevated sections, concrete barrier walls/expressway, banked bends, on/off-ramp connectors, "minimal low-speed technical content") is NOT found in any source — mapmaster does not mention "C1," "elevated," "expressway," or "banked." Those are plausible real-world-Tokyo-informed embellishments, not sourced facts. They do not contradict the high-speed profile, but they overstate what the sources actually verify; the high-speed classification itself rests only on the sourced word "full-throttle" plus the S1-800 class.

tracks.name: Legend Island Circuit
tracks.character: Dedicated multi-lap sealed-asphalt circuit on the fictional endgame Legend Island. In-game description: "challenging turns and blazing fast pace." Community sources call it "the best high-speed asphalt track in the game," built for R-class hypercar pace (Valkyrie, Exige WTAC) with a high-speed rhythm that rewards clean lines. So: fast, top-end-relevant, but with genuine corners (not a highway blast like the island's Colossus/Goliath). Notably "punishes unstable tuning setups" — stability/traction matter. NOT documented in any source: turn-by-turn geometry (hairpin count, chicanes), elevation profile, or wall/barrier layout — do not assume these.
tracks.length: ~8.8 mi total, 3 laps (~2.9 mi/lap), R class (998 PI)

research.caveat: Residual real-vs-in-game and precision risks: (1) The exact in-game event description "challenging turns and blazing fast pace" could not be verified verbatim in any fetched source — its substance (turns + speed) is corroborated, but treat the literal quote as unconfirmed. (2) Two of the sources the claim cites for CHARACTER actually don't support it: the EZG blog only covers Legend Island as a region and forza.labsgg only lists format (type/laps/distance); neither describes driving character. The character support genuinely comes from mitchcactus and 2upskill/mmogah instead. (3) A minority of (AI-summarized) sources call it "highly technical" / rewarding "precise driving over raw speed," so the degree of top-end bias carries some uncertainty — plain "mixed" is a defensible fallback if the fast-lean is overstated. (4) Turn-by-turn geometry, elevation, and barrier layout remain undocumented, as the claim correctly states.

tracks.name: The Goliath
tracks.character: Dominated by long freeway/highway straights (top-end matters, "build your lead") but broken up by technical mountain-pass sections with tight switchbacks/hairpins that "punish late braking," plus coastal sweepers and elevation change. Predominantly tarmac; a couple sources claim minor off-road/city segments (unverified, conflicting). City/highway walls present. Class R 998 "Track Life," summer/clear/afternoon. Starts on Legend Island (SE corner of Japan map).
tracks.length: ~53.1 mi single lap (some guides state ~50 mi / ~80 km); one full perimeter loop of Japan, ~20-25 min per lap

research.caveat: Franchise-pattern vs in-game mismatch risk: a "Goliath" (longest map-looping circuit mixing highway with other roads) exists in every prior Forza Horizon, so the "freeway + technical mountain mix" profile may be pattern-matched from the series template rather than FH6's actual layout. The FH5-Mexico hallucination in one aggregator shows sources conflate titles. The route's EXISTENCE and general highway-dominant character are well attested for FH6, but the specific "mixed-fast" profile and feature list are inferred from a non-independent SEO cluster, not verified against a primary in-game source; distance and several features are wrong or unconfirmed.

tracks.name: The Colossus
tracks.character: Single closed "highway loop" on the NE side of Shimanoyama. Character = long full-throttle highway straights/sweepers where top speed dominates; community gameplay report: "basically zero low speed corners, only high and mid speed, and super long full throttle segments." A handful of high/mid-speed corners plus a few hard braking zones next to highway walls/barriers ("hit the wall hard or brake almost to a standstill"); NO low-speed hairpins. Dry tarmac, Summer / Clear / Early Afternoon. Speeds reported ~420 kph / 300+ mph on the straights.
tracks.length: 23.4 mi, 1 lap, ~7 min (verbatim mapmaster.io + labsgg agree). NOTE: some blog/wiki sources claim ~50mi/80km whole-map loop — treated as conflation with a Goliath-style event, not the Shimanoyama Colossus.

research.caveat: Real-world/prior-game mismatch risk is high: "The Colossus" and "The Goliath" are recurring Forza-tradition endurance names (FH4/FH5), and the FH6 guide web is (per this project's own methodology note) dominated by SEO/AI-generated tier-lists that copy each other and may be importing FH5's Colossus/Goliath characteristics rather than describing FH6's actual route. The most trustworthy signal is the Steam player testimony (independent of the SEO cluster), which supports a fast-but-technical mixed-fast route with hard braking zones — not a pure high-speed straight-line event. Fundamental facts still conflict across sources (length 23.4 vs ~50mi; lap time ~7 vs 20-25min), so treat even the confirmed 23.4mi/high-speed-loop details as probable, not settled.

tracks.name: Festival Sprint
tracks.character: Tarmac point-to-point that runs straight through the open Horizon Festival Site grounds (flat, wide plazas) then exits "out the other side" into surrounding Ohtani roads. FH6-source description emphasizes speed/flow and scenery ("speeds right through"), pointing to fast sweepers and momentum sections rather than a tight-hairpin touge. Surrounding Ohtani terrain includes forested elevation/mountain roads (evidenced by the neighboring Festival Chase event) plus wide festival flats, so expect some elevation change and a few medium corners bridging the fast sections. No confirmed hairpin count, wall/barrier density, or turn-by-turn layout in any source. Surface: tarmac (Road Racing category, not dirt/street).
tracks.length: ~4.9 mi, 1 lap (point-to-point)

research.caveat: Real-world vs in-game mismatch risk is LOW here (the description references the in-game Horizon Festival Site, not a real place), but the route text is marketing/flavor copy, not a corner-by-corner analysis, so the "mixed" (medium-corner) half of mixed-fast is inferred — partly from the neighboring "Festival Chase," which forza.labsgg.com actually classifies as a Street race (different discipline), a weak bridge. Minor source discrepancies: region is labeled "Ohtani" (mapmaster) vs "Horizon Festival" (labsgg) — consistent since the Festival Site sits in Ohtani; and labsgg lists no car restriction while mapmaster specifies B600 Super Hot Hatch — a gap, not a contradiction. To upgrade PLAUSIBLE to CONFIRMED, verify actual corner character against in-game footage or a leaderboard ghost.
sources: https://www.gosunoob.com/forza-horizon-6/ (Festival Sprint Super Hot Hatch tune guide, B600 confirmed via search index)

tracks.name: Tokyo Railway Sprint
tracks.character: Urban Tokyo City street course in the southern Minamino region. Corner-dominated: the event's own description says it "requires on-rails cornering ability to get ahead of the pack," so grip/braking/rotation through street corners is the differentiator rather than top-end. Asphalt/road surface, city-street setting (expect 90-degree junctions, medium straights between blocks, and close barriers/walls typical of urban FH6 courses). "Railway/on-rails" is thematic wordplay — no source confirms the route physically hugs a rail line, though elevated Tokyo rail scenery is plausible. Not a hairpin crawl: an S2 leaderboard WR of 1:45.3 over 4.2 mi (~144 mph avg) implies meaningful flowing/fast sections between the technical corners. Elevation not documented.
tracks.length: 4.2 miles, point-to-point sprint (single run, no laps)

research.caveat: Real-world-vs-in-game mismatch risk is HIGH on the CHARACTER (not the metadata): "on-rails cornering" is wordplay on the track name "Railway," and the corner-dominance is bootstrapped from that pun rather than any layout source — exactly the name-inference failure mode. The 4.2 mi / ~144 mph S2 average is real hard evidence that argues the course carries meaningful speed, so the true profile could be mixed-technical (as claimed) OR mixed-fast; "mixed" is the central estimate. To actually confirm, watch the WR/gameplay footage (e.g. youtube.com/watch?v=olG4GInYVPw) and count technical corners vs sustained straights. The DB entry should stay character_confidence="inferred"/"probable" — not upgraded to a verified in-game route character.

tracks.name: Shikisai Sprint
tracks.character: Route (from mapmaster.io, describing the actual FH6 event): "Cut a winding path through the Hokubu Region and under the highways before looping back." So: predominantly winding/twisty asphalt with tight-to-medium corners, passing UNDER highway overpasses (underpass detours, not high-speed highway driving), then looping back toward the start. Surface: asphalt (confirmed by forza.labsgg). Region: Northern Hokubu, documented (via the Hokubu Time Attack guide) as "technical" with "tight corners" that "favor high-downforce builds over pure top speed." Class restriction: A-700 Modern Super Saloons (heavier sedan platforms). Conditions: Spring / Clear / Late Afternoon. No explicit source data on hairpin count, elevation change, or walls specific to Shikisai.
tracks.length: 4.8 miles, 1 lap, point-to-point sprint (loops back near start)

research.caveat: Confirmation rests primarily on one specialist site (mapmaster.io) for the Shikisai-specific route text; I did not analyze actual gameplay footage (BMW M4 '21 and "how to find" YouTube videos exist but were not watched) to independently count corners/straights over the 4.8 mi. The "technical" region evidence comes from a DIFFERENT Hokubu event (S1 circuit Time Attack), so it is region-level, not Shikisai-specific. Minor terminology tension: it is billed as a SPRINT yet mapmaster says "looping back" and labsgg says "1 lap" — not a speed-profile contradiction, but worth noting. The precise "weighted toward grip/handling" nuance vs neutral "mixed" is interpretive; the route text supports a technical lean but a hidden faster connecting section over 4.8 mi cannot be fully excluded without footage. Given the project's own caution that much FH6 guide content is SEO/AI-generated, treat the CONFIRMED verdict as high-but-not-absolute; the per-event uniqueness and the explicit no-high-speed-flag are what lift it above PLAUSIBLE.

tracks.name: Coastline Sprint
tracks.character: Two-part coastal sprint. Technical/twisty first half through the Nangan Region (rewards precise braking, sweeping asphalt curves, ocean-side), transitioning to a flat-out high-speed back half running toward Tokyo City (rewards top-end/raw horsepower). Surface: paved asphalt throughout. Corners are described as "sweeping" curves, not tight hairpins; no explicit mention of hairpins or heavy elevation. Start grid sits on the coastal edge in the SW corner of the map.
tracks.length: 5.0 miles, 1 lap (point-to-point sprint)

research.caveat: Provenance is community-tier fan sites (mapmaster.io + u4n.com), not a Forza-primary source or the player's own in-game leaderboard/screenshot. The event blurb may be mapmaster.io's editorial phrasing rather than a literal verbatim in-game string, so the claim's "quoted verbatim" / confidence="verified" framing is slightly stronger than the evidence class strictly warrants — best treated as probable-to-verified. Either way the description is grounded in the actual traced in-game route (a route-mapping site), so the "mixed" character holds. The project's own rivals-tracks.json scope note that mapmaster.io provides "names/regions/format only" is inaccurate — the site does carry per-event narrative descriptions.

tracks.name: Satta Sprint
tracks.character: FH6 in-game description reads: "A flat-out charge through the Ito Region to really test your nerve and control at top speeds" — i.e. dominated by long full-throttle sections where top-end and high-speed stability matter, not tight cornering. Runs through the southwestern side of the Ito region. Set in Summer, Clear weather, Sunrise. Real-world namesake (Satta Pass, Shizuoka) is a coastal/elevated pass above the Tomei Expressway and Suruga Bay, consistent with sweeping high-speed road, but in-game specifics on walls, exact elevation and sweeper geometry are NOT explicitly documented in the sources found.
tracks.length: 5.1 miles, point-to-point, 1 "lap" (single run)

research.caveat: Real-world-vs-in-game note: the actual Satta Pass (Satta Toge, Shizuoka) is a narrow, winding viewpoint road, so a name-based guess could plausibly have read "technical" — the "high-speed" characterization comes specifically from the FH6 in-game blurb, not the real place, which is good but means name and reality diverge. Source-depth note: the route-CHARACTER claim (high-speed) rests essentially on mapmaster's single in-game blurb; labsgg and guides4gamers confirm the event/format/length/restriction but do not independently describe driving character, and gameplay footage was not frame-verified for corner geometry. Confidence in high-speed is strong but the speed-profile corroboration is effectively single-source. In-game specifics on walls, exact elevation, and sweeper geometry remain undocumented in the sources found.

tracks.name: Venus Sprint
tracks.character: Narrow, twisting mountain road climbing from Takashiro (NE side) up toward the Sotoyama region — net uphill elevation gain. Tight switchbacks/hairpins with guardrail-lined drops (walls close, low run-off) characteristic of the Takashiro pass (FH6's Mt. Haruna / Initial D analogue), transitioning near the top into the alpine gateway where hairpins are separated by some longer straights/sweepers. Tarmac surface, Spring/Clear/Early Afternoon (dry grip). Forced car class: A-700 "Total Muscle" (heavy, high-torque, RWD-stock).
tracks.length: 5.0 miles, 1 lap (point-to-point sprint)

research.caveat: Real-world/adjacent-track mismatch risk: the "mixed" straights/sweepers and the Initial-D/Mt-Haruna hairpin framing come from the real Takashiro-to-Sotoyama geography and the neighboring Sotoyama alpine event (tateyama-kurobe-sprint), NOT from any FH6 description of Venus Sprint's own layout. Only a thin general blurb ("narrow, twisting mountain road") exists; no source details corners/straights/elevation. Venus Sprint sits on the Takashiro side, so the alpine sweepers the claim invokes likely belong to the adjacent track. YouTube gameplay of the route exists but was not frame-verified, so a faster mid-section cannot be fully ruled out — hence technical is the best-supported label, with mixed-technical only a generous upper bound.

tracks.name: Ito Sprint
tracks.character: Coastal point-to-point along the eastern coast of the Ito Region. Described as "twists and turns along the coastal roads" — winding, corner-dominant character (cornering/grip emphasis, NOT a top-end course). No hairpins, elevation, sweepers, or walls are explicitly specified by sources; coastal seawalls are likely but unconfirmed. Surface: open asphalt. Class S1 800 Modern Supercars; Summer/Cloudy/Morning; requires Orange Wristband Access. Deliberately contrasted by the guide with the nearby Satta Sprint (a "flat-out charge at top speeds"), confirming Ito Sprint is the technical/cornering event of the two, not the high-speed one.
tracks.length: 5.8 miles, 1 lap (point-to-point)

research.caveat: Real-world-vs-in-game mismatch was the original risk and it resolved in the claim's favor: the dropped "mountain" trait was the name-inference, and it was correctly removed. Two residual cautions. (1) The "technical" CHARACTER rests primarily on mapmaster.io's single descriptive sentence; forza.labsgg only corroborates distance/laps/type, not the prose. The exact sub-label ("mixed-technical" vs plain "technical") is a judgment call on a 5.8-mi coastal road that likely has flowing sections — profile is confirmed at the character level, not turn-by-turn, and finer features (hairpins, seawalls, elevation) remain unconfirmed as the claim itself states. (2) Naming-confusion hazard for future passes: FH6 also has a separate "Ito Half-Mile" DRAG event in the same area — do not conflate it with the "Ito Sprint" road race.

tracks.name: Shimanoyama Sprint
tracks.character: Coastal/shoreline roads on the SW side of the Shimanoyama region — predominantly fast, flowing sealed tarmac ("flat-out coastal sprint"). Punctuated by at least one "very sharp right turn" that is the main hard-braking/technical pinch point. Mild elevation from adjacent inland hills; no street-circuit walls (this is open road, distinct from the Shimanoyama Charge street race and the Shimanoyama drift Circuit). Class S2 900 "Extreme Track Toys"; Summer, Clear Post-Rain, Late Afternoon conditions. Runs as a Road Racing event unlocked via Purple/Launch Control wristband.
tracks.length: ~4.0 miles, 1 lap (point-to-point sprint)

research.caveat: Both corroborating sources are third-party community/guide databases (mapmaster.io, forza.labsgg.com), not the official Forza site, so residual risk of database inaccuracy remains. The place name literally means "island mountain," which would naturally mislead toward a mountain/touge profile; the coastal reading depends on trusting the in-game route blurb over the name. One WebFetch summary also loosely mentioned "mountain driving," and "mild elevation from adjacent inland hills" is plausible, but the dominant character per sources is coastal/fast, keeping mixed-fast (not high-speed, not technical) the best fit.
sources: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=5pTw3Hx4iB0 (FH6 How to Find Shimanoyama Sprint Road Race Location)
https://game.wiki/forza-horizon-6/shimanoyama-region (region page; returned 403 on fetch, referenced via search snippet describing coastal terrain)

tracks.name: Seaside Park Sprint
tracks.character: Coastal/seaside point-to-point sprint along the southern coast of Ito that passes through Legend Island. Per the only detailed in-game route description (mapmaster.io): "a mix of flat-out speed and sudden tight turns demand the driver's full focus" — i.e., fast coastal straights/sweepers punctuated by abrupt tight corners. Tarmac surface; coastal roads (likely barriers/walls, but not confirmed). Elevation profile and specific hairpin/sweeper counts NOT documented by sources. Restriction: Hypercars (S2 900). Conditions per mapmaster: Summer, cloudy, dawn.
tracks.length: 4.5 mi, 1 lap (point-to-point)

research.caveat: The descriptive route blurb rests on a single source (mapmaster.io); labsgg corroborates only the metrics, not the wording. No source quantifies corner/sweeper counts, hairpin count, or elevation, so the exact sub-flavor is not pinned down — the route could lean "mixed-fast" (long coastal straights with a few punctuating tight corners) rather than evenly mixed, though "sudden tight turns... demand the driver's full focus" argues against a top-end-dominant read. The "S2 900" class detail in the claim is an inference from the "Hypercars" restriction (mapmaster/labsgg state "Hypercars" without an explicit numeric PI cap). No frame-by-frame gameplay-video verification of the actual driven line was performed; verdict rests on the official in-game event description plus corroborated metadata.

tracks.name: Tateyama Kurobe Sprint
tracks.character: Alpine route in Sotoyama with real elevation change; passes through the Tateyama Kurobe "Snow Corridor" = narrow section flanked by snow walls (punishing, low runoff). Mix of fast straights/sweepers (high average speed) plus a technical switchback/snow-corridor pinch that forces braking. Tarmac/asphalt surface. Runs roughly east-west through a valley.
tracks.length: 3.8 mi, 1 lap (point-to-point sprint)

research.caveat: Residual risks: (1) The event's OWN restriction is S2-900 Hypercars, not S1 — the 1:39.763 is an S1 Rivals-leaderboard time, so "S1 world-record" is a class leaderboard, not the event restriction, and "hotlap" is loose wording for a point-to-point sprint. (2) The in-game descriptor "fast-paced" is promotional flavor text and no source characterizes the corner-by-corner difficulty; the "technical pinch" half of mixed-fast is partly inferred from the real-world Snow Corridor, leaving mild uncertainty between "mixed-fast" and "high-speed." (3) Real-world Tateyama Kurobe Alpine Route is a bus/trolley-only switchback road and the real Snow Corridor (Yuki-no-Otani) is a fairly straight walled walking section, so FH6's version is a fictionalized driving interpretation — but this cuts in the claim's favor (in-game plays faster than the name implies), so real-world-vs-in-game mismatch risk is low. (4) Per this project's own methodology note, much of the FH6 guide web is a self-copying SEO/AI cluster; here the cross-corroboration by the official forums, labsgg map data, and a video WR mitigates that.

tracks.name: Irokawa Space Centre Drag
tracks.character: Short straight-line drag (~quarter mile). Launch + first-gear traction decide it far more than top speed.
tracks.length: ~0.2-0.25 mi (near 1/4-mile; the paired Drag Meet is the classic Quarter Mile)
tracks.strip_bias: SHORT — launch-dominated; AWD hooks hardest; SHORTEST gearing. The launch IS the race here.

drag_playbook.approach: Apply the DRAG discipline template (Tuning Templates tab). HIGH-convergence discipline: the tune is a formula — don't hunt per-car codes, apply the template and tune GEARING to this strip.
drag_playbook.gearing: SHORTEST — maximise off-the-line accel; you won't reach top speed. Hit the limiter late.

car_by_class.S2 (850): Mazda MX-5 Miata FE (BEST; medium acq — aftermarket reload-spawn 500k) or Nissan GT-R Black Edition FE (hard — Wheelspin/AH). Both 10.0 launch/accel.
car_by_class.S1: Nissan GT-R NISMO (AWD) — or build up the standard non-FE 2012 GT-R Black Edition (Autoshow 80k) into an S1 drag spec.
car_by_class.A and below: Meta still forming (FH6 is young). RULE: pick the car in your class with the best Speed / Acceleration / LAUNCH stats, favor AWD for the launch, and pick a PI-efficient chassis — then apply the drag template. (Send me a class board and I'll pin the exact car.)

drag_playbook.launch: The launch is ~everything on a short strip. Rev to peak torque, feed throttle to balance bog-vs-spin; AWD = be aggressive. Practice the reaction + first shift.
drag_playbook.confidence: verified (template + S2 cars); lower-class per-car picks = probable (meta forming)

tracks.length: 0.5 mi (half-mile)
tracks.strip_bias: MEDIUM — balances launch and top-end; MEDIUM gearing. Both AWD launch and power-to-weight matter.

drag_playbook.approach: Apply the DRAG discipline template. HIGH-convergence: apply the formula, tune GEARING to this strip length.
drag_playbook.gearing: MEDIUM — reach the limiter in top gear right at the line; balance accel vs terminal speed.

tracks.character: 1 km straight-line drag. Longest strip -> top-end power + gearing dominate; pure-launch cars lose their edge.
tracks.strip_bias: LONG — top speed + LONGER gearing matter most; the launch matters least of the three (still don't fluff it). Light/RWD + aero-min can beat launch-only cars.

drag_playbook.gearing: LONGER — you have room to reach a high terminal speed; don't over-shorten or you'll top out early.
